title: P-11: setId-first + symmetric-mount convention tripwire — no-set-singletons.test.js guards against re-singletoning a seam and against reinstating a root mount
recipe: No recipe covers convention tests. The script is SIBLING-SET-PLAN.md §5 P-11 (BOTH assertions — the setId-first rule and the R7 symmetry rule), §4.3 (the `prefix = '/' + setId` scheme) and §7 T-10; the FORM is the existing fs-walk convention test src/server/app/copy-convention.test.js — read it first and mirror its structure (node:fs readdirSync + node:url fileURLToPath + a describe with a 'Should find the …' guard case before the real assertions).

filesToTouch.what:
A cheap, mechanical tripwire so a future increment cannot quietly reintroduce a single-slot seam after pp-056 removed them all.

WALK: the L2 directories model/, bridge/, flow/, engine/ and services/ under src/server/app, recursively, collecting every .js file that is not a .test.js. Use the same idiom as copy-convention.test.js — `readdirSync(dir, { recursive: true, withFileTypes: true })` (or the plain recursive form plus a path join, whichever the repo's Node version and existing file use) and `fileURLToPath(new URL('./model', import.meta.url))` for the roots, so the test is location-independent.

RULE: read each file's source and find every exported function whose name starts with `configure`. For each one, assert its FIRST PARAMETER IS NAMED `setId`. Match the declaration forms the codebase actually uses — `export const configureX = (setId, …) =>` and `export function configureX(setId, …)` — with a regex over the source text; this is a convention test, not a compiler, and a source-text match is both sufficient and the cheapest thing that cannot rot. If a configure* export is found whose first parameter is not setId, FAIL with a message naming the file, the export and the parameter it found, so the failure is self-explaining without opening the test.

GUARD CASE FIRST (copy-convention.test.js precedent): an `it('Should find the configure seams')` asserting the walk discovered at least the seven known seams by name — configureObligationSet, configureFulfilmentRegistry, configureJourneyFlow, configureRecords, configureSession, configureCommodityReference (and buildDispatch, see below). Without that guard, a broken walk that finds NOTHING passes vacuously, which is the classic way a convention test dies silently.

buildDispatch: it is a seam with the same setId-first contract but does not match the configure* name pattern. Include it as an explicit named check in the same file rather than widening the regex (widening would sweep in every build* helper in the codebase and produce false positives).

ALLOW-LIST: an empty array, exported as a named const at the top of the file with a comment saying it is empty BY DESIGN and that adding an entry means a seam has been exempted from co-residency — which is a decision, not a fix.

SECOND ASSERTION — THE R7 SYMMETRY TRIPWIRE (added by ruling R7; the file now guards TWO invariants). In the same file, a second describe: register EVERY gateway the app exports — import them from `src/server/app/routes.js` and register them against a booted Hapi server exactly as router.js does (at THIS increment routes.js is still the un-split live-animals gateway, so that is one gateway; drive the test off the module's exports rather than a hardcoded list, so pp-006's barrel and pp-007's `plantProducts` export are covered automatically with NO edit to this file) — and then assert, over `mountedSetIds()` and the registry: (a) NO set is mounted at prefix '' (and, defensively, `registerSetMount(id, '')` throws); (b) every registered prefix matches `/^\/[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$/` — one lowercase segment, no nesting, no trailing slash; (c) every registered prefix is EXACTLY `'/' + setId` for its own set id, which is the whole scheme in one line and the only assertion that cannot drift. Fail with a message naming the set id and the offending prefix. Guard case first, same rule as the seam walk: assert the registry discovered AT LEAST ONE mount, so a boot that silently registered nothing cannot pass vacuously.

WHY THIS SECOND ASSERTION EXISTS: R7 reversed FD-16's asymmetric scheme (live-animals at the root, plant-products prefixed). Without a mechanical guard, a later increment can quietly reinstate it — and the asymmetry is not merely untidy, it HIDES a bug class: with a set at '', a doubled prefix and a dropped prefix produce the same correct-looking string for that set, so the fault only ever surfaces on the other set, in code that set's suite never runs. Keeping every set off '' is what keeps both mistakes visible on the first request.

NO dependency-cruiser rule accompanies this: the constraint is about a function's parameter shape, which dep-cruiser cannot express. That is exactly why a convention test is the right instrument here.

TWO steps now cite this tripwire, not one (R7). Step 4 of the recipe (write the L1 gateway) already points at it per pp-053: verify it does, and correct it to name the file exactly as shipped — `src/server/app/no-set-singletons.test.js` — and to state the seam rule in one sentence: every configure* seam takes setId as its first parameter, the allow-list is empty by design, and a new seam that cannot take setId is a co-residency decision to raise, not a test to exempt. STEP 1 (choose the set id) must ALSO cite it, for the symmetry rule: the mount prefix is not a choice, it is `'/' + setId`; no set owns `/`; and this test fails the build if a set is registered at '' or at anything other than `'/' + setId`. Naming it in step 1 is what stops the next author from 'just taking the root because ours is the main journey'. If pp-053's text already says both things correctly, make no edit and drop the file from the diff.

specs: src/server/app/no-set-singletons.test.js — IS the deliverable; it is a convention test, not a test of new behaviour.
acceptanceCriteria: src/server/app/no-set-singletons.test.js walks model/, bridge/, flow/, engine/ and services/ under src/server/app and fails any non-test .js file that exports a configure* function whose first parameter is not named setId.
It additionally pins buildDispatch's setId-first contract by name, without widening the configure* regex to build*.
It is GREEN on pp-056's output with an EMPTY allow-list — no seam needs an exemption.

It is RED if setId is dropped from any seam: prove this during the increment by temporarily removing setId from one seam's signature, watching the test fail with a message naming that file and export, then reverting. Record in the commit message that the red was observed — a tripwire never seen red is a tripwire that may not work.

R7 SYMMETRY ASSERTION: with every gateway routes.js exports registered, no set is mounted at prefix '', every registered prefix matches /^\/[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$/, and every registered prefix equals '/' + its own setId. The test is driven off routes.js's exports, so pp-006's barrel and pp-007's plantProducts gateway are covered with no edit to this file.

It is RED if any set is registered at '' or at a prefix that is not '/' + setId: prove this too, by temporarily changing one registerSetMount call, watching the named failure, and reverting. Both reds are recorded in the commit message. This is the guard that stops a later increment quietly reinstating the asymmetry FD-16 reversed — and with it the doubled/dropped-prefix bug class that an empty prefix hides.

A vacuous pass is impossible on EITHER assertion: one guard case asserts the walk discovered the seven known seams by name, and a second asserts the mount registry discovered at least one mount, so a broken walk or a boot that registered nothing fails loudly instead of finding nothing and going green.
The failure message names the file, the export and the offending parameter name.

It follows the fs-walk idiom of copy-convention.test.js (node:fs readdirSync, fileURLToPath-based roots, a 'Should find …' guard case first) so it reads as idiomatic to this codebase rather than as a foreign gadget.

docs/add-a-set.md steps 1 AND 4 name this file and state their respective rules (step 1 the symmetric-mount rule, step 4 the setId-first rule), so the next set's author meets both before writing their gateway.
No dependency-cruiser rule is added and .dependency-cruiser-known-violations.json is not regenerated.
npm test, npm run test:live-animals and npm run lint are green; no existing suite's test count drops; no production file is edited by this increment.
verification: npm --prefix ~/git/defra/trade-imports-animals/repos/trade-imports-animals-frontend test  # baseline BEFORE editing — red baseline = stop and report
notes:
AMENDED FOR RULING R7 (Sam, 2026-08-01, later session). The file now guards TWO invariants, not one: the setId-first seam rule (R3) and the SYMMETRIC MOUNT rule (R7 — every set at `'/' + setId`, no set at ''). SIZE stays S: it is one more describe in the same file, and both assertions are cheap source-level/registry-level checks. SEQUENCING NOTE: dependsOn grows to pp-057, because the symmetry assertion needs the mounts to actually be `'/' + setId` — pp-056 declares the mount, pp-057 makes it real; running this tripwire before pp-057 would assert a scheme the app is not yet serving.

RULING R3 (Sam, 2026-08-01) makes co-residency a standing property of the platform, not a one-off migration. pp-056 keyed every seam by set; this increment stops the keying from decaying. It is deliberately the cheapest thing that works — a source-text convention test — because an expensive guard gets deleted the first time it is inconvenient.

WHY A CONVENTION TEST AND NOT A LINT/ARCH RULE: dependency-cruiser reasons about MODULE GRAPHS. The constraint here is about a FUNCTION'S PARAMETER SHAPE, which dep-cruiser cannot express at all. ESLint could in principle, via a custom rule, but a custom rule is a package, a config entry and a maintenance surface; the fs-walk convention test is a pattern this codebase ALREADY uses (copy-convention.test.js, copy-parity.test.js), so it is idiomatic and needs no new tooling.

SEQUENCING: it lands immediately after pp-056 and BEFORE the gateway split (pp-006), so that nothing from the gateway work onwards can re-singleton a seam. SIBLING-SET-PLAN §9 phase m0-a puts it at step 4, after P-10 (pp-057) and before P-4/P-3 — dependsOn is pp-056 AND pp-057: the seam rule needs the keyed seams to be green against, and the R7 symmetry rule needs the mounts to be real, which is pp-057's doing.

EXEMPLAR (read first): src/server/app/copy-convention.test.js — verified live this session; it imports readdirSync from node:fs, path from node:path and fileURLToPath from node:url, builds its root with `fileURLToPath(new URL('./sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features', import.meta.url))`, filters directory entries, uses `readdirSync(dir, { recursive: true })` for the deep walk, and opens its describe with an `it('Should find the feature folders')` guard asserting the walk found something. Mirror all four of those choices.

THE SEVEN SEAMS the guard case must name (from SIBLING-SET-PLAN §4.2 rows 1-7): configureObligationSet (model/obligations/manifest.js), configureFulfilmentRegistry (bridge/fulfilment-registry.js), configureJourneyFlow (flow/journey-flow.js), buildDispatch (flow/dispatch.js — named separately, see filesToTouch), configureRecords (engine/persistence/records.js), configureSession (engine/persistence/session.js), configureCommodityReference (services/persistence/records/notification-mapper/commodity-reference.js).

OBSERVE THE RED. The single most common failure mode for a tripwire is that it never actually fires. The acceptance criteria require temporarily breaking one seam's signature, seeing the named failure, and reverting — do it, and say so in the commit message.

SCOPE FENCE: this increment adds ONE test file (plus at most a one-paragraph doc correction). It edits no production file. If the walk finds a genuine violation in existing code, that is pp-056 work that leaked — report it rather than fixing it here, so the fix lands with the increment that owns the seam.
openQuestions: Whether to also assert the mirror-image rule — that no L2 file declares a module-level mutable binding intended as a seam slot (`let configured…`, `export let …`). It would catch a re-singletoning that avoided the configure* name entirely. Planned as NOT in scope: the regex would be noisy against legitimate module state (caches, memos) and a noisy tripwire gets disabled. Raise it again only if a real regression slips through the parameter-shape rule.

Whether services/ is too broad a walk root — it contains set-agnostic session/records implementations that have no configure* exports, so it costs only walk time today. If it ever produces a false positive, narrow the root rather than adding an allow-list entry; an allow-list entry means a seam was exempted from co-residency, which is a decision for Sam.
